The [original NextItNet implementation](https://github.com/fajieyuan/WSDM2019-nextitnet/blob/master/ops.py) uses left-only causal padding, biased convolutions, channel-only LayerNorm, and residual addition. Implementation implication: mask embeddings and re-mask internal activations before every temporal convolution; masking only block outputs allows convolution biases or LayerNorm offsets at padded positions to enter later valid positions. Preserve the baseline’s normalization/activation/dropout order, then apply the mask after that positionwise processing, before the next convolution. For a residual gate, use y = mask × (x + gate(x) × F(x)), gating the completed residual branch after its activation/dropout and before addition. Compute gates positionwise, without temporal pooling; normalization must not aggregate across sequence positions.

Recommended checks, inferred from these dependencies: with dropout disabled, changing future tokens must leave earlier features unchanged; gradients from output t to inputs after t must be zero. Compare identical histories with different amounts of left padding, aligning valid positions: features and scores should match within numerical tolerance. Hook every internal convolution input to assert padded activations are zero, and perturb masked embedding values to verify valid outputs remain unchanged. Exercise nonzero convolution biases and LayerNorm offsets, multiple blocks/dilations, and short histories. Causality alone cannot detect leakage from past padded positions. Read out the final nonpadding position—L−1 for nonempty, strictly left-padded histories.

For y = x + sigmoid(Wx+b)F(x), W=0 and b=2 give sigmoid(2)=0.880797: residual contributions shrink about 11.9%, so initialization is not baseline-equivalent. Random gate weights also make the initial gate input-dependent. Exact equivalence requires an initially unit multiplier, for example sigmoid(Wx+2)/sigmoid(2) with W=0; this permits multipliers above one. [Residual-gating reference](https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/highway-networks.html).
